# WilsonSpeak Remotion Slide Pack

Create short, premium 16:9 Remotion insert animations for WilsonSpeak long-form videos. Treat these as supporting graphics between real footage, screen recordings, and narration, not as a full motion-deck replacement for the video.

## Output Contract

Default to the WilsonSpeak external project folder:

`/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/render/<slide_pack_slug>/`

Create:

- `src/`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and `remotion.config.ts`
- `renders/` with one MP4 per composition plus a full preview MP4
- `qa/` with still frames for visual inspection
- Optional `slide_pack_notes.md` only when Wilson needs a human-readable clip list

Render settings:

- 16:9 horizontal, `1920x1080`, `30fps`
- H.264 MP4, `yuv420p`
- No audio by default; these are insert graphics for the main edit
- Individual clips usually `5-8s`; full preview can concatenate all clips

## Template

Prefer starting from `assets/remotion-slide-template/` when it exists. Copy it into the project render folder, then edit text, timing, colors, and compositions to fit the requested topic.

If `node_modules` is missing:

1. Reuse an existing local Remotion `node_modules` symlink when available, especially `/Users/wilsondenq879/Documents/Codex/2026-06-16/shorts-ollama-remotion/node_modules`.
2. Otherwise run `npm install` in the slide-pack folder, requesting network approval if needed.

Keep `remotion.config.ts` on PNG image frames:

```ts
Config.setVideoImageFormat('png');
Config.setOverwriteOutput(true);
```

JPEG intermediate frames can produce `yuvj420p`; if `ffprobe` shows `yuvj420p`, switch to PNG and rerender.

## Slide Families

For a workflow explainer, produce 5-7 compositions:

1. `Hero`: the main thesis, e.g. manual workflow to Codex workflow.
2. `ManualWorkflow`: old process, friction points, repeated manual steps.
3. `TimeCostStack`: where time is spent; show stacked bars or structured cost blocks.
4. `AssistMap`: how Codex participates across the workflow.
5. `SkillPipeline`: personal rules or SOP becoming a reusable skill.
6. `TakeawayCard`: one concise closing idea or quote.
7. `FullSlidePack`: a preview composition that sequences all clips.

Adapt names to the topic, but keep the family coverage unless Wilson asks for fewer clips.

## Visual Standard

Use WilsonSpeak long-form styling:

- Traditional Chinese on-screen text and Taiwan wording.
- Editorial, restrained, work-focused visuals; avoid a startup-pitch or keynote-template feel.
- Dark matte or quiet neutral background with purposeful accent colors.
- Use stable dimensions and explicit positions so text does not shift or collide.
- Use clear typography hierarchy: small kicker, large thesis, smaller supporting copy.
- Keep bottom subtitle area clear; avoid bottom progress bars, lower-thirds, or persistent bottom cards.
- Use cards for individual process nodes only. Do not stack cards inside cards.
- Avoid gradient blobs, bokeh, decorative orbs, generic AI imagery, and filler icons.
- Prefer process maps, charts, before/after panels, and clean workflow diagrams.
- Make each slide useful even if it is only on screen for a few seconds.

## Animation Rules

- Drive all animations from `useCurrentFrame()` and `useVideoConfig()`.
- Use `interpolate()` with clamped easing; prefer `Easing.bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for crisp UI entrances.
- Use fades and small translate/scale moves; avoid noisy motion.
- Time entrances by semantic order: headline first, then nodes, then connector lines or emphasis.
- Leave enough hold time after the final state for viewers to read.
- Keep transitions clean with fade-in/fade-out; no hard cuts inside a clip unless intentional.
- Hard rule for visual stability: Remotion slide packs must not visibly jitter, shimmer, or wobble. Use fixed card/text dimensions, deterministic layout constants, stable source image sizes, and rounded/integer pixel positions for x/y/width/height/crop values. Avoid per-frame text measurement/reflow, random/time-based values, fractional crop coordinates, and tiny continuous pan/zoom moves that stutter at 30fps.
- If a camera move, chart grow, or product/image movement is needed, animate with one simple eased transform and settle into a stable hold. Do not stack multiple subtle transforms on the same element when a static hold or fade is enough.

## Workflow

1. Confirm the target project folder or infer it from Wilson's prompt.
2. Create a dedicated slide-pack folder under `render/`.
3. Copy the template or scaffold a minimal Remotion project.
4. Write compositions around the requested narrative beats, not generic feature labels.
5. Run `tsc --noEmit`.
6. Render stills for each composition at meaningful mid/late frames.
7. Inspect stills visually. Fix text overflow, node collisions, line crossings, cramped right edges, and subtitle-zone conflicts.
8. Render each composition to `renders/*.mp4` plus a `full-slide-pack.mp4` preview.
9. Run `ffprobe` on representative clips and the full preview.
10. Play the rendered MP4s at 1x and scrub around animation starts, chart motion, image movement, and final holds. Fix any vibrating text, product photo wobble, axis/card jitter, or one-frame layout shift before delivery.
11. Report the composition list, render paths, and QA status.

Useful commands:

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
./node_modules/.bin/remotion still <CompositionId> qa/<name>.png --frame=<frame> --scale=0.5
./node_modules/.bin/remotion render <CompositionId> renders/<name>.mp4 --codec=h264 --pixel-format=yuv420p
ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height,pix_fmt,r_frame_rate -show_entries format=duration -of default=nw=1 renders/<name>.mp4
```

## QA Bar

Before delivery, verify:

- `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- Each selected still has readable text and no overlap.
- Rendered clips play without visible jitter, shimmer, text/card wobble, or product/image shake.
- The bottom subtitle area remains clear.
- Lines and arrows do not pass through important text.
- MP4s are `1920x1080`, H.264, `30fps`, and `yuv420p`.
- The full preview exists and plays through all slide families.
- The output lives in the requested WilsonSpeak project folder, not only in the temporary Codex workspace.

Create WilsonSpeak-style YouTube Shorts using the approved WilsonSpeak workflow.

- Treat `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/outputs/final.mp4` as the canonical final deliverable. Versioned revisions should live in the same `outputs/` folder, e.g. `<project_slug>_v2.mp4`. `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_codex_output` is legacy only; do not use it for new Shorts unless Wilson explicitly asks.

- For Shorts material selection, treat index fields as edit constraints: prefer `aspect_label=vertical_9x16` for native vertical素材, accept `horizontal_16x9` only with intentional blurred-fill/foreground framing, and prefer `quality_score >= 65` (`good` or better) for primary B-roll. Use lower-quality素材 only as brief context or when Wilson approves the tradeoff.

If Codex just downloaded/captured/generated a file for the current project, use its known path directly and let the weekly index pick it up later unless Wilson asks otherwise.
- BGM lives in `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_bgm`.
- Use only Wilson-provided BGM from `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_bgm`; do not browse, download, generate, or substitute external BGM.
- Default BGM choice is `monks` unless Wilson explicitly asks for another provided BGM track.
- Reusable WilsonSpeak Shorts tools live in `/Users/wilsondenq879/Documents/Codex/wilsonspeak_tools/shorts_pipeline/`. For future Shorts work, read this folder first and reuse its scripts instead of recreating per-project render/TTS/QA code.
- Per-video project working files must live on the external Transcend drive under `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/` by default.

## Shorts Production Notes

Carry these forward as practical WilsonSpeak Shorts defaults unless Wilson asks otherwise.

- For vertical Shorts that use horizontal or mixed-aspect footage, keep the foreground video vertically centered. Do not anchor the foreground clip too high. The safe default is true center placement, equivalent to FFmpeg overlay logic like `overlay=(W-w)/2:(H-h)/2`.
- When using blurred-fill vertical framing, treat the sharp foreground clip as the subject layer and keep equal headroom/footroom unless the shot clearly requires a different crop.
- For AI, software, platform, and product-strategy Shorts, choose official footage that visually proves the narration: keynote stage moments, product demos, app UI, device screens, software/hardware interface operation, workflow execution, or hands-on device interaction. Prefer Apple/Google/OpenAI/Anthropic official videos and developer/keynote clips over generic lifestyle advertising.
- Hard rule for Remotion/chart animation reuse: do not repeat the same Remotion animation or chart composition for more than one narration beat in a Short unless Wilson explicitly asks for a chart-led slideshow. If a chart is needed for adjacent lines, use it once for the strongest data beat, then cut back to official footage, product/demo footage, or a different visual. Avoid showing the same Remotion animation again at later timestamps such as a second appearance around `40s` and `56s`.
- Hard rule for cards over Remotion: when the current visual source is a Remotion animation, chart, comparison graphic, or overlay-heavy motion graphic, do not add a separate section card or punch card on top. Let the Remotion graphic and subtitles carry the point. Use cards only on footage-led beats where the card adds emphasis without duplicating an existing animated chart.
- Hard rule for Remotion-only or Remotion-primary Shorts: if Remotion is the primary foreground visual for a narration beat, `cards` must be empty for that beat. If Remotion is the primary visual for the whole Short, `video_manifest.json` must use `cards: []`, and `card_sync_report.json` must be exactly `[]`.
- Hard rule: Remotion compositions used in WilsonSpeak Shorts must not include progress bars, timeline bars, countdown bars, editor/debug timecode, or fake player UI unless Wilson explicitly requests that exact device/player treatment.
- Hard rule: do not cut one mostly-static Remotion composition into repeated per-segment source ranges to fill narration. Use one continuous Remotion render once through `continuous_source_id`, or create distinct Remotion scenes/real B-roll. Reusing the same static Remotion/material source as repeated segment material is a loop/replay reject even if `source_start` differs slightly.
- For Remotion foreground plus background material-video layouts, both layers must be non-looping. The foreground Remotion render must run forward continuously for its intended duration, and the background material must use a forward-only source range with no replay, clone, freeze, or loop.
- Remotion data visualization quality gate: study the RemotionLab showcase before designing. Avoid grid backgrounds, heavy rounded cards, nested panels, colored outline boxes, fake UI chrome, and decorative lines framing information. Let the data marks carry the design: line/area paths, bullet bars, dot flows, range lines, small multiples, and typographic numbers.
- Remotion text-density gate: do not turn data beats into verbose Remotion text cards. Keep one headline, sparse labels, and one source note. If the beat is a same-prompt comparison, prefer the actual two prompt/result screenshots or screen-recording crops over a synthetic字卡 that restates the prompt.
- Remotion transition gate: do not add fade-in/fade-out to every screen-recording cut or every short Remotion section. Use simple cuts for screen evidence and reserve fades/ease transitions for true section changes.
- Remotion timing gate: data reveals, screenshot changes, and comparison highlights must not visibly lead the narration. If Wilson says the picture is ahead of the voice, rebuild timing from the TTS/subtitle events and align visual reveals to the spoken point.
- Perceptual repetition is also a reject. A static or slow-moving webpage, repo page, chart, screenshot, or local素材 split across adjacent subtitle events can still feel looped even when `source_start` changes. If one visual must support one spoken thought, render it as one continuous shot, or use continuous `source_start` with boundary fades/restarts disabled. Otherwise cut to a different source or intentionally hold a still frame without fake motion/replay.
- When adjacent timeline entries use the same source path and continuous source time, the renderer/manifest must preserve continuity at the boundary, for example `fade_out=false` on the first entry and `fade_in=false` on the next. QA `render/shot_timeline.json` or the equivalent render plan before delivery.
- Remotion title/header safe area is mandatory. Persistent header/title text must sit below mobile/player crop boundaries; for 1080x1920 Remotion outputs, keep it at least as low as `WilsonSpeak y=132` and main title `y=174`, and lower it further when screenshots show top-edge clipping. QA must inspect a first-scene frame and reject the render if any top title is clipped by a black boundary or player crop.
- Avoid using generic ad-only scenes, crowds, pets, unrelated people-at-home moments, abstract logo loops, or mood footage when the narration is about agentic workflows, models, UX, app intents, device ecosystems, or software/hardware interfaces. If such footage appears in an official clip, skip to a more relevant timestamp or use a different source.
- When matching B-roll to a segment, first ask what the viewer should learn from the image. If the shot does not reinforce the specific spoken point, downgrade it to filler and replace it with UI/demo/keynote/interface footage whenever available.
- Material QA is mandatory before final export. For each important narration beat, inspect representative frames from the chosen source timestamp and reject the shot if it only supplies brand mood, unrelated lifestyle context, crowds, pets, or generic advertising. The accepted frame should visibly show the thing being discussed: app UI, command flow, assistant response, device screen, product operation, keynote demo, interface control, developer workflow, or a clearly relevant hardware/software interaction.
- Text-density QA is mandatory before final export. Sample every webpage/screenshot/card beat and reject frames where background text competes with Chinese subtitles or card copy. Stacked text layers such as webpage text plus source label plus card plus subtitles are a hard reject unless Wilson explicitly asks for a source-document style edit.
- Hard rule: do not loop any material to fill time in WilsonSpeak Shorts. No official footage, local B-roll, screen recording, Remotion render, chart video, still-image pan, or generated clip may be replayed, cloned, frozen, or looped as a visible repeated segment unless Wilson explicitly asks for a deliberate replay. If a source clip is too short for the narration beat, cut to a different timestamp, different material, official footage, a new chart/visual, or shorten/split the beat. Repeated visible material at different timestamps, such as the same shot appearing around `20s` and `1:17`, is a hard reject.
- Before final export, audit the timeline for repeated source path plus repeated source timestamp/range. Reject the render if any material range is reused as filler, even if subtitles, section cards, or overlays differ.
- When Wilson supplies a new YouTube or official material URL, download the raw file into the appropriate folder under `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_materials`, use the known downloaded path directly for the current edit, and note reusable timestamps in `planning/material_plan.md`. Do not rerun the global materials index immediately unless Wilson asks for `素材index` or the new material must be discoverable by search before selection.
- After rendering, sample QA frames at every replacement material beat and at any segment Wilson previously questioned. Do not rely on the manifest label alone; visually confirm that the actual rendered frame matches the narration and that renderer timing/concat behavior did not leave a previous unrelated shot on screen.
- HDR/SDR mixed-source QA is mandatory for official keynote footage. Run `ffprobe` on important sources and the canonical final output. If any source is HDR, e.g. `bt2020`, `smpte2084`, `arib-std-b67`, or 10-bit `yuv420p10le`, verify that the installed FFmpeg build has a tested, color-correct HDR-to-SDR path before using it. Do not merely force BT.709 tags or rely on a generic `colorspace` chain: a PQ source can become cyan/purple while the output still reports BT.709. When the required color-managed filter is unavailable, choose a verified SDR official alternative or create a verified SDR intermediate; then re-render every affected Short. Compare a source frame and its rendered counterpart at the same timestamp whenever a color shift is suspected. The final Short must report video `pix_fmt=yuv420p`, `color_space=bt709`, `color_transfer=bt709`, and `color_primaries=bt709`, with HDR mastering/content-light side data removed.
- For UI/product/interface-heavy Shorts, use a higher-quality render setting than generic B-roll. Prefer reusable renderer defaults around H.264 CRF 18 or equivalent; avoid very low bitrate outputs that make UI text, keynote slides, or device screens mushy after YouTube re-encoding.
- For home-network, product-demo, and explainer Shorts, prefer real footage first: ports, cables, hands plugging in devices, indicator lights, living-room usage, and device closeups. Use generic context shots only when they cannot be mistaken for the exact named product.
- For Shorts that explain a concept rather than announce a keynote, visuals should teach: closeups of ports, actual cabling direction, device role, and user-symptom shots such as buffering or unstable playback.
- Named-object visual accuracy is mandatory, not optional polish. When narration names a device, accessory, or control surface, choose footage that visibly matches that object category: Apple TV should show Apple TV, a TV interface, Siri/TV remote, Ethernet, Thread/smart-home context, or living-room TV use; Google TV Streamer should use Google TV/generic streaming, remote, smart-home, or TV-interface context and must not imply Apple TV footage is Google TV; router/Wi-Fi beats should show routers, ports, cables, signal/coverage, app/network UI, or household network symptoms. Reject generic hand, keyboard, abstract data, or unrelated lifestyle shots if a closer local素材 or official/source visual exists.

## Direct Research And Planning

Codex owns the complete planning pass: source research, thesis and hooks, narration, frame plan, material plan, EDL, overlay copy, and metadata. When a project is started, consolidate the work into `planning/approval_pack.md`, `planning/source_notes.md`, `planning/material_plan.md`, `narration.txt`, and `video_manifest.json`.
- For AI infrastructure, semiconductor, and platform-strategy explainers, use one or two custom evidence/diagram clips when local B-roll cannot teach the mechanism. Keep diagrams text-light, subtitle-safe, and source-grounded; do not stack a section card over a diagram.
- Before render, run a manifest/source audit that rejects repeated `(path, source_start)` pairs, visible loop/replay, tail clone/freeze fills, and adjacent text-heavy evidence shots that compete with subtitles.
- When Vibe/Sona/ProArt transcription has recognition errors, use it only for timing. Remap its start/end times back to exact Traditional Chinese `narration.txt`, keep `exact_text_match=true`, and store the raw recognizer output next to the clean exact SRT/timeline for audit. After remapping, validate that every event has positive duration, event boundaries are monotonic, and the final event ends no later than the actual TTS duration from `ffprobe`. If one recognizer clause covers several approved subtitle events, split only inside that clause using phrase or text-length boundaries; do not repeatedly snap unrelated events to the nearest global ASR boundary, which can create zero-duration tail shots or timestamps beyond the audio.
- Use explicit `display_text` line breaks for important terms and mixed-language phrases. Do not ship broken terms such as `Jalapeñ o`, `agent 工 / 作流`, `full / -stack`, split product names, orphan Chinese fragments, or awkward English hyphen breaks.
- When Wilson asks for `完整字幕`, every spoken clause must appear as a caption sequence; a summary/punch-caption track is not sufficient. Keep the exact spoken text in the timing event, allow display normalization only for readable technical notation (for example, `M 五 Pro` → `M5 Pro`), and manually line-break model identifiers such as `千問 2.5 72B` before export. Inspect these mixed CJK/number captions in the rendered MP4 because automatic wrapping can split decimal model names even when the subtitle report passes.
- After the first render, inspect default QA frames plus manual frames for every custom diagram, every card, and any long or manually line-broken subtitle. If a frame reveals overlap or bad wrapping, update only the display text/layout when narration is unchanged, then re-render.
- For graphic-led Shorts, allocate exclusive vertical zones before drawing: a top title zone, an explanatory-graphic zone, a small source-label zone, and the subtitle band. Do not keep a persistent title when each graphic already carries its own header; that duplicates text and creates collisions. Treat the subtitle region as unavailable to chart copy, labels, decorative bars, and data tiles. On a 1080x1920 canvas using the standard `y=1210-1518` subtitle band, keep custom-graphic text above about `y=1160` and source labels around `y=1120` or higher. This rule applies equally to white and dark backgrounds.
- When custom graphics are involved, QA every unique graphic as well as the final subtitle frames. Check full-canvas renders—not only cropped contact sheets—for clipped glyphs, elements hidden by a subtitle-safe mask, graphic text under the subtitle box, and persistent-header collisions. If the design uses a white or light background, switch title/source text to a dark palette with sufficient contrast rather than retaining white-on-dark overlay defaults.
- In the final response, embed the local final MP4 with absolute Markdown media syntax when useful, e.g. `![title](/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/outputs/final.mp4)`, and state clearly whether upload has or has not happened.

## Subtitle Tooling

- Keep `narration.txt` as the only source of truth.
- Preferred subtitle pipeline for WilsonSpeak Shorts is: approved `narration.txt` -> one-pass ElevenLabs TTS WAV using the configured model and voice ID -> open the WAV in the Vibe desktop app -> set language to `Chinese` -> click `Transcribe` -> export/copy `srt` timing -> save a reviewed Traditional Chinese `.srt` inside the project `audio/` folder -> only then start video rendering from that `.srt` source of truth.
- Use the Vibe desktop app as the default SRT timing tool, not the bundled `sona` CLI, when a desktop session is available. Launch with `open -a /Applications/vibe.app <project>/audio/<narration>.wav` so Vibe loads the exact project WAV and does not reuse a same-named cached file from another project.
- Vibe may return Simplified Chinese, recognition errors, or a tiny hallucinated duplicate tail at the end. Treat Vibe output as timing only: map its start/end times back onto the exact approved `narration.txt` Traditional Chinese text, remove any hallucinated duplicate tail, and save the clean timing as `<project>/audio/<name>_vibe_exact_zh_tw.srt`.
- WilsonSpeak Shorts deliverables must not ship Simplified Chinese subtitles, even if Vibe returns Simplified Chinese by default.
- Generate subtitle events from exactly `narration.txt`, then render punctuation-clean display text from those events. Do not hand-rewrite subtitle wording after timing is set.
- For reusable `wilsonspeak_tts.py`, default to one ElevenLabs TTS call for the full `narration.txt`, using `ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID=eleven_v3` and the configured `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID`. Do not synthesize each subtitle segment separately, because per-segment TTS can return noticeably different voice color or delivery. If ElevenLabs is unavailable, use the Google/Gemini fallback as one full-narration call.
- Subtitle segments are production units, not just script paragraphs. Keep each segment short enough to fit the approved Shorts subtitle band. If a segment would exceed 4 visible subtitle lines, split it before TTS. The renderer must fail rather than truncate text.
- Hard rule: the approved `.srt` must be generated from the final TTS WAV with Vibe before render begins. Do not start Shorts rendering from text-weight estimates, guessed segment durations, Whisper-only timings, or hand timing when the Vibe desktop app is available.
- The approved `.srt` must exist before render begins. Do not start Shorts rendering until the Vibe-generated, remapped Traditional Chinese subtitle file has been generated and accepted as the timing source of truth.
- For batch Shorts where the Vibe desktop app is impractical and Sona/CLI transcription is used, treat the recognizer output as timing only. Remap recognizer start/end times back to exact `narration.txt`, write both the raw recognizer transcript and the clean exact Traditional Chinese SRT/timeline, and mark the timing source explicitly, e.g. `vibe_sona_remapped_exact_zh_tw`. Reject any final render whose subtitle timeline source is `estimated`, `text_weight`, proportional duration, hand timing, or unknown.
- The base visual render should stay subtitle-free. Burn subtitles only in the final subtitle pass from the reviewed `.srt`, so subtitle timing/layout can be revised without rebuilding the whole edit.
- Preferred approach is exact ASS subtitle generation so timing, placement, stroke, and safe-area behavior are deterministic. Reuse `scripts/generate_exact_ass.py` as the starting point when possible.
- For new Shorts, prefer the reusable root helper `wilsonspeak_generate_exact_ass.py` when available. Provide a per-topic JSON config with `segments`, `aligned_times`, and optional `cards`, then generate both `subtitles.ass` and `subtitle_alignment_report.json` from the same source.
- Subtitle timing must be aligned to the rendered single-take TTS waveform. Use Vibe-generated timings by default; use text-weight estimates only as a temporary fallback, then snap boundaries to nearby quiet audio valleys and reject the output if visual/audio QA shows noticeable lead or lag.
- Do not use a global negative subtitle offset to "feel synced". If subtitles appear before the voice, fix the segment timings from the TTS audio. The approved default render delay is `TEXT_DELAY = 0.0`.
- Visible Shorts subtitle text must remove sentence punctuation such as `。`, `，`, `：`, `？`, `！`, commas, and trailing quote/bracket marks. Keep the spoken text exact in the timeline and verification report so `exact_text_match` still reconstructs `narration.txt`.
- For WilsonSpeak Shorts, subtitles must be burned into the local video render and Shorts upload packages must not include SRT/captions by default. Use YouTube upload subtitles only for long-form videos or if Wilson explicitly asks.
- Before export, always produce an exact-match subtitle report and visually inspect at least: first subtitle, one long two-line subtitle, one card transition, and the ending subtitle. Inspect against audio playback, not still frames alone.

## BGM Selection Notes

- Use only Wilson-provided BGM from `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_bgm`.
- If Wilson specifies an exact track, use that exact track instead of the default.
- If Wilson does not specify a track, default to `monks`.
- For explainers and how-to Shorts, prefer neutral instrumental tracks that stay out of the narration's midrange. Avoid busy melodic hooks, strong vocals, or overly bright/percussive tracks that fight consonants.
- For upload-ready mixes, narration clarity is more important than musical energy. On phone-speaker style playback, if model names, acronyms, numbers, or technical terms are even slightly masked, lower the music again.
- Practical default: keep BGM roughly in the `volume=0.10-0.14` range before final loudness normalization, then verify by ear. This is the current WilsonSpeak default because the older `0.05-0.08` mix was too quiet.
- If Wilson explicitly asks for a louder Shorts-style BGM mix, increase music in controlled steps and preserve sidechain ducking under speech. The cloud-gaming sample used a louder approved revision with FFmpeg-style parameters around `BGM volume=0.22`, narration `volume=1.75`, `sidechaincompress=threshold=0.02:ratio=10:attack=20:release=320`, and `amix=inputs=2:weights=1 0.78`, followed by `alimiter=limit=0.95`. Use this louder mix when Wilson asks for BGM to be more present, then verify consonants and technical terms remain clear.

## Approved Voice

Use ElevenLabs TTS by default with Wilson's configured model and voice ID:

- Primary provider: ElevenLabs text-to-speech.
- Required model: `ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID=eleven_v3`.
- Required voice: `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` from the shared/project `.env`, chosen by Wilson. Do not replace it with a default ElevenLabs voice unless Wilson explicitly asks.
- Load `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID`, and `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` from `.env`; never print API keys.
- Google/Gemini fallback: if ElevenLabs is unavailable because of API/network/quota/permission issues, fall back to Gemini TTS using `GEMINI_API_KEY` and voice `Orus`, then continue the same one-pass TTS, Vibe timing, and QA workflow.
- Default speed: normal/original speed. Do not post-process with FFmpeg `atempo` unless Wilson explicitly asks.
- Style target: professional Taiwan Mandarin male market-analyst voice, about 40-50, steady, restrained, medium-low to low, judgment-oriented, like an investment-program or morning-meeting read.
- Keep diction clear, mature, logical, and professionally paced. Do not use a casual youth voice, exaggerated short-video hype voice, overly bright tech-review voice, or theatrical delivery.
- Future WilsonSpeak Shorts narrations default to ElevenLabs `eleven_v3` with Wilson's configured `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` unless Wilson explicitly asks for another voice/provider.
- For market, stock, semiconductor, AI infrastructure, product strategy, and supply-chain topics, always prefer the professional market-analyst delivery: calm, restrained, judgment-oriented, and closer to a morning-meeting or investment-program read. Avoid ad-like hype, over-performed short-video cadence, and every-sentence-upward intonation.
- Before generating TTS, audit acronyms, product names, model names, event names, and letter-number combinations that may be misread or blended by TTS. Rewrite the spoken `narration.txt` into pronunciation-safe text while keeping the visible title/subtitles natural when needed. Examples: write `WWDC 26` as `W W D C 二十六` for speech, spell single-letter acronyms with spaces, and separate dense English/number strings so the voice does not merge them into an unintended Chinese word or sound. Verify the first occurrence by listening before final export.
- Before TTS, also audit money, specs, and units with a `raw -> spoken -> visible` pronunciation map. Do not feed raw ambiguous values to TTS. Taiwan price narration should sound natural: `NT$84,900` -> `台幣八萬四千九` or `台幣八萬四千九百元`; `NT$184,900` -> `台幣十八萬四千九` or `台幣十八萬四千九百元`; `$2,499` / `2499` -> `兩千四百九十九` with the currency/context stated. Reject TTS that misreads values such as `2499` as `1499`.
- Normalize bandwidth units for speech: `GB/s`, `GByte/s`, and `GBps` should be spoken as `gigabyte per second`; `Gbps` should be `gigabit per second`. Keep official unit text in visible subtitles/cards when helpful, but use spoken-safe text for TTS.

To avoid unnecessary paid TTS usage, do not call ElevenLabs or Gemini TTS during planning, rough layout, storyboard drafting, subtitle drafting, or edit iteration. Call TTS only once the edit plan has passed Wilson approval and the subtitle/video layout has passed local QA. If a later script change is required, regenerate TTS only after Wilson confirms the revised transcript. A confirmed rewrite requires the complete chain again: updated `narration.txt` and visible text, one new TTS take, a new local timing pass, reviewed exact SRT/timeline, render, and QA; never retain timings from the superseded narration.

If both ElevenLabs and Google/Gemini TTS are unavailable, stop and explain the blocker instead of silently substituting another voice.

## Approval Gate

Before generating TTS or doing the final export, show Wilson these three artifacts and wait for explicit confirmation:

1. `大綱`: the short's thesis, 2-4 beats, limitation/counterpoint, and takeaway.
2. `逐字稿`: the exact narration text that will become `narration.txt`.
3. `Frame 對照草圖`: a beat-by-beat frame/storyboard table mapping each narration segment to planned visual source, subtitle/card text, approximate timing, and any B-roll/keynote/product asset.

Do not proceed to final editing, TTS generation, or final export until Wilson approves these artifacts. If Wilson asks for changes, update the three artifacts and ask again.

## Script Retention Check

Use the `youtube-scriptwriter` style only as a planning checklist, not as a separate replacement for WilsonSpeak's approval gate. For original Shorts built from ideas, research notes, news, or raw transcripts, create or update `planning/script_retention_check.md` before showing the approval packet.

- Define the exact viewer, the viewer problem or curiosity gap, the core WilsonSpeak thesis, and what the Short will make clearer than a normal recap.
- Generate `3-5` hook options, then choose the one that is both retention-strong and source-grounded. Do not choose a hook only because it sounds shocking.
- Score the script's `shock/novelty` on a simple `1-5` scale and write the evidence behind the score. A high score without official/source support is a rewrite trigger, not a reason to exaggerate.
- Choose an explicit short-form structure, such as `hook -> context -> mechanism -> impact -> limitation -> takeaway`, then make sure every beat earns its place.
- For Shorts longer than about `70s`, include one mid-video rehook or tension reset before the viewer's attention drops. This can be a concrete number, tradeoff, contradiction, or "why this matters now" turn.
- Run a comprehension audit before TTS: a viewer should understand the thesis, mechanism, and takeaway without seeing the sources. If the script needs too much background to follow, simplify the argument before making visuals faster.
- Close by looping back to the opening tension or giving Wilson's analytical takeaway. Do not add generic "like/subscribe" CTAs unless Wilson explicitly asks.

`smartcut` is useful only as an optional source-prep tool for cutting long source videos into project-local selects with minimal recoding around cut points. It must not replace the normal WilsonSpeak Shorts render, vertical framing, subtitle burn-in, BGM ducking, HDR-to-SDR normalization, or final QA.

- Use it only when `smartcut` or the Smart Media Cutter CLI is already available, or when Wilson approves installing/running it. The open-source GitHub repo says it is no longer updated as of February 2026, so treat it as convenience tooling, not a required dependency.
- Good uses: pre-trim a long official keynote, demo, screen recording, or local material into a short source clip under the project folder before the final FFmpeg/Remotion pipeline.
- Poor uses: final Shorts export, clips that need crossfades/overlays/crops, subtitle timing, BGM mix, audio cleanup, or any edit where the final picture must be rebuilt anyway.

## Strict Text Rule

Use one source of truth:

1. Write `narration.txt`.
2. Generate subtitle text segments from exactly the same text, but do not call TTS yet.
3. Generate TTS from exactly `narration.txt`, but only after Wilson approves the outline, transcript, and frame storyboard, and after the silent/draft video, subtitle layout, and card layout have passed local QA.
4. Before output, verify that subtitle segments joined together equal `narration.txt` after whitespace normalization.

Do not summarize, omit, rewrite, or shorten subtitle text after TTS has been generated. If the script changes, regenerate both TTS and subtitles.

When changing terminology across a project, scope the edit to narration, visible text, titles, and approved script fields. Preserve source URLs and official citation identifiers verbatim; never apply a blind global text replacement across Markdown links or research references.

Subtitle sync must be judged against the rendered voice, not just text equality. Exact text reconstruction is necessary but not sufficient. Before delivery, inspect several subtitle transitions against the audio, especially long clauses, numbers/specs, and the first 20 seconds. If subtitles visibly lead or lag the narration, regenerate timing using a more precise segmentation method or shorten/rebalance subtitle chunks before export.

Bad subtitle wrapping is a hard reject. Do not ship captions that split a semantic phrase into an orphan line or broken word, such as `工作邊 / 界`, `更重 / 的情況`, or `也被 / 吃掉`, and do not split useful English phrases such as `rate limit` in a way that hurts reading. Fix this by splitting the subtitle event at nearby TTS pauses or by setting explicit `display_text` line breaks; never fix it by changing the spoken text after TTS.

## Timing And Layout QA

- Treat narration, subtitles, and title/punch cards as one synchronized timeline. Subtitle events must reconstruct the narration exactly, and title/punch cards must be derived from those subtitle events whenever possible.
- Every final WilsonSpeak Short must include a short opening safety preroll before the first spoken syllable so the first word is not clipped by local players or YouTube decoding. Default: add `0.35s` at the start by cloning/holding the first video frame and delaying the full mixed audio by `350ms`. If applying this after subtitle burn-in, pad the already-subtitled picture and delay the audio together so visible subtitles remain aligned. Equivalent FFmpeg pattern:

```text
[0:v]tpad=start_duration=0.35:start_mode=clone,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[v];
[0:a]adelay=350:all=1[a]
```

- If the renderer builds timing from source events before burn-in, alternatively start all subtitle/card/audio events after the same `0.35s` preroll and render the first frame as a silent hold. Either approach is acceptable as long as the first audible word is preserved and subtitle sync remains correct.
- Do not place a major title or punch card earlier than the first subtitle event that says the matching idea. A card may start slightly after the matching subtitle start, but never before it.
- Do not place section cards or punch cards on narration events whose visual source is a Remotion chart/animation. This is a hard reject because it creates duplicate text layers and makes the frame feel like two slides at once.
- Before delivery, generate or inspect a card-sync report with: card text, matched subtitle text, subtitle start, card start, and a boolean proving the card does not start early.
- Subtitle position must be visually checked, not assumed. Primary Chinese subtitles should sit low and close to the bottom safe area, but must not collide with English subtitles, bottom crop edges, main title cards, or important faces/products.
- If Wilson says subtitles are faster than TTS, treat it as a timing bug and rebuild the subtitle timing from TTS pauses. Do not solve it by moving cards or changing visual timing only.
- Subtitle sync QA must include audio playback against the final rendered MP4, not only exact-text reports or still frames. For batch output, run a per-video timing audit and inspect at least the first 20 seconds, one middle long clause, and the ending. If subtitles lead/lag the TTS or cards feel synced to guessed text timing instead of speech, rebuild timing from the final TTS audio and re-render every affected Short before upload.
- Numbered/key-point subtitles must be checked against the rendered TTS, not just the event start time. If `第一 / 第二 / 第三` or a similar list is shown as one multi-line caption, it must start at or just after the narrator reaches the first item and remain visible long enough to read all lines. Reject the export if the whole list appears before the voice reaches it.
- Section cards and punch cards should not be vertically centered by default. Place cards in the upper foreground, around `y=260` on a 1080x1920 canvas, so they avoid covering the main foreground subject and lower subtitles.
- Approved drawtext/PNG defaults for WilsonSpeak Shorts: `TEXT_DELAY = 0.0`, `CARD_Y = 260`, persistent title safe area at about `WilsonSpeak y=132` and main title `y=174`, and the subtitle band fixed above the YouTube Shorts lower UI around `y=1210-1518`. Use a white Heiti TC font, heavy black stroke, and semi-transparent black subtitle/card boxes.
- Prefer the reusable root style helper `wilsonspeak_short_text_style.py` when available. It contains the approved subtitle wrapping, subtitle box style, card box style, and upper-card placement.
- For every export, inspect representative frames at: first subtitle, every card start after 0.2-0.4 seconds, a long two-line subtitle, and the ending subtitle. Reject the export if text appears too early, overlaps incoherently, covers the subject's face, or falls outside the safe viewing area.
- For every export, inspect representative frames for material repetition. Reject the export if the same visible source shot, same source timestamp range, same Remotion chart animation, or same generated/still visual appears more than once as filler.
- For every Remotion export, explicitly QA: no progress/timeline/timecode/debug UI, no cards over Remotion, no repeated/looped Remotion or background material ranges, no frozen/clone-filled Remotion tail, and no clipped top header/title.
- For every Remotion data visualization export, also QA against `references/remotionlab-dataviz.md`: extract stills/contact sheets for every Remotion scene and reject grid backgrounds, odd colored frames, nested cards, text-heavy字卡, unbalanced empty space, subtitle/label collisions, repeated Remotion loops, and visual reveals that run ahead of narration.
- For every export, include at least one QA frame for each long subtitle and each explicit multi-line subtitle. Reject the export if any line break creates an orphan fragment, splits an important term, or forces readers to parse a sentence in the wrong order.
- For section-card videos, also inspect at least three frames around one card transition: before/early fade, mid fade, and full card. Reject the export if the card or blurred background appears as a hard cut.
- If the project used the `sona -> .srt` path, QA must verify the reviewed Traditional Chinese `.srt` itself, the no-subtitle base video, and the final subtitled export. Do not inspect only the final MP4 and assume the subtitle source file is correct.

- Subtitle box:
  - Draw a semi-transparent black rounded rectangle.

Overlay generation method:

- Preferred implementation: use Pillow to create transparent PNG overlays, then FFmpeg to composite them.
- Generate:
  - `overlay_pngs/title.png` for the persistent WilsonSpeak label and main title.
  - `overlay_pngs/sub_00.png`, `sub_01.png`, etc. for each subtitle event.
  - Optional `card_00.png`, etc. only if Wilson explicitly wants cards.
- Build an `overlay_specs` list:

```text

fade=t=in:st=<start>:d=0.25:alpha=1,
fade=t=out:st=<end-0.45>:d=0.35:alpha=1[ovN];
[previous][ovN]overlay=0:0:enable='between(t,<start>,<end>)'[vN]
```

## Approved v8 Keynote Style

Use this as the default style for keynote, product launch, NVIDIA, Apple, AMD, Microsoft, Google, AI infrastructure, semiconductor, and supply-chain commentary unless Wilson asks for another look.

- Reference feel: Apple Mei-style keynote recap, adapted for WilsonSpeak. Do not copy another creator's footage or exact edit; use official keynote/product footage, press assets, and Wilson-owned materials.
- Structure: 60-90 seconds, clear hook, 3 concrete beats, practical investor or tech takeaway.
- Narration: more口語短影音, less report-like. Prefer lines such as "表面上是在講 X，但真正重點是 Y", "第一個關鍵", "所以我會這樣看". Keep Taiwan Mandarin professional, but conversational.
- Visual base: real keynote footage and product/demo footage first. Use black vertical canvas with 16:9 keynote footage framed as a clean stage window when the source is horizontal. Avoid pure chart/card slideshow.
- Main title: show a persistent or recurring title in the upper half of the video, large and obvious. Recommended format:
  - Line 1: product/event name, e.g. `NVIDIA GTC 2026`
  - Line 2: literal thesis, e.g. `重點不是 GPU，是 AI 工廠`
- Subtitles: place Traditional Chinese subtitles low and close to the bottom safe area, with a smaller English line underneath when it fits. Use high-contrast white text, strong dark stroke/background, and avoid covering the main keynote subject.
- Punch cards: use short 2-line cards as rhythmic emphasis near the upper-middle area, not as full subtitle replacements. Examples: `AI 代理 / 自己執行`, `Vera Rubin / 整櫃平台`, `少看口號 / 多看出貨`.
- Punch-card timing is mandatory QA: cards must be tied to subtitle/narration events and must not appear before the narrator reaches the matching idea. Generate or inspect a card-sync report before delivery; reject the export if any card starts earlier than its matched subtitle event.
- Title/card placement must adapt to the shot. On speaker closeups, avoid face and upper torso; place cards either high in unused negative space or lower-middle above subtitles. On slide/product shots, upper-left or upper-middle cards are acceptable if they do not cover the key visual.
- Source label: show a small source label only on official keynote clips, e.g. `Source: NVIDIA GTC Keynote 2026`.
- Color/style: mostly black, white text, restrained accent color from the brand when useful, e.g. NVIDIA green. Avoid busy gradients and decorative UI.
- Delivery: export `1080x1920`, `yuv420p`, under 2 minutes. Verify that video duration covers full TTS duration and does not truncate the ending.

## Depth Standard

WilsonSpeak Shorts can be fast, but they must not be shallow. For tech, AI, semiconductor, market, supply-chain, platform, and product-strategy topics, use this depth standard by default.

- A Short must have a real thesis, not just a recap. Prefer a judgment such as `這不是單一產品新聞，而是 PC 角色被重新定義`, `表面是硬體升級，真正壓力在軟體生態`, or `短期不會取代雲端，但會改變開發與採購決策`.
- Every script should answer at least 3 of these 5 questions: what changed, why now, who benefits, who is pressured, and what limitation or counterargument still matters.
- Use a fast structure with analytical depth: hook, context, mechanism, impact, limitation, takeaway. In a 60-100 second Short, each part can be 1-3 sentences, but none of them should be empty hype.
- Include causal language. Use `因為`, `所以`, `真正關鍵是`, `這會逼`, `短期看`, `長期看`, `但限制是` to make the reasoning explicit.
- Avoid shallow lines that only restate specs, slogans, or brand claims. If mentioning specs, immediately explain why that spec changes behavior, cost, workflow, ecosystem control, or competitive pressure.
- Include at least one tension or tradeoff when the topic is strategic: cloud vs local, CPU vs GPU, open ecosystem vs closed stack, performance vs cost, developer adoption vs hardware capability, or short-term sales vs long-term platform shift.
- Do not dilute depth just to increase pace. Speed comes from concise writing and quick visual cuts, not from removing the reasoning.
- Before generating TTS, run a mental script audit: if the narration can be summarized as only `產品很強、產業會改變、大家要注意`, rewrite it with concrete mechanism and consequence.

## Wilson Reference-Calibrated Analytical Shorts

Wilson's baseline for AI, Mac, platform, and purchase-decision Shorts is the structural standard demonstrated by the supplied reference [`Mac mini M6 的 32GB 夠跑 AI 嗎？`](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/5B6cCk67aLE), an approximately 86-second vertical analysis. Use this standard when Wilson asks for the usual high-quality WilsonSpeak Short, unless he explicitly asks for a quick update or a shorter format.

- Target roughly `75-95` seconds when the topic needs a real decision or analysis. The duration must earn its time through new evidence and a useful conclusion; do not stretch a thin news recap with filler.
- Start with one concrete viewer question, constraint, or decision in the first `3-6` seconds. State the named product, number, or scenario immediately, so viewers know what answer they will get.
- Build one continuous argument: decision question → mechanism or limiting factor → two to four sourced facts → practical consequence → clear recommendation, tradeoff, or decision rule. For product topics, include price, availability, configuration threshold, or workload boundary when that changes the answer.
- Every factual block must answer the opening question. Specs only stay when the narration explains how they change model capacity, cost, speed, workflow, or buying choice.
- Plan `8-14` purposeful visual beats across a ~90-second Short. Use product images, device operation, official UI/keynote evidence, brief readable data comparisons, and source-grounded price or configuration moments. Generic AI stock footage can support transitions only; it cannot carry the central argument.
- Design the cover around one dominant proof point or decision threshold, a short reader-facing question, and an accurate product image. Keep the hierarchy immediate: one large number or constraint, then the product and question. Do not copy the reference's artwork, typography, footage, or wording.
- Keep spoken cadence measured enough for a Taiwan Mandarin viewer to absorb numbers and terms. Use concise clauses, deliberate pauses before the verdict, and visible subtitle holds that let a configuration, price, or comparison be read.
- During approval, show the expected duration and a beat map proving the middle contains evidence, visual change, and decision value. Reject a script that only offers an announcement, a list of specs, or a generic conclusion.

## Approved Section-Card Template

Use this fixed template for keynote, product launch, NVIDIA, Apple, AMD, Microsoft, Google, AI infrastructure, semiconductor, and supply-chain Shorts unless Wilson explicitly asks for a different look. This is based on the approved `gtc2026_rtx_spark_pc_industry_impact_v6_visible_fade_cards.mp4` result.

- Opening: do not show a large section card at the start. Start with source/keynote footage, one-line top title, and low subtitles.
- Main title: one unboxed line near the top, e.g. `NVIDIA RTX Spark：PC 產業衝擊`. Do not put the persistent title inside a rounded rectangle.
- Source label: small text above or near the title, only when using official keynote/product footage, e.g. `Source: NVIDIA GTC Taipei 2026 keynote`.
- Section cards: show only true section cards for the main beats, usually 2-3 cards such as `高階 PC / 變本地 AI 平台`, `CPU 廠壓力 / 開始變大`, `雲端不消失 / 個人端變重要`.
- Timing: do not show a section card until the narration truly enters that section. Never use the opening hook as a section card. Remove extra punch cards that merely repeat specs or closing takeaways unless Wilson asks for more.
- Card layout: place the card in the upper foreground rather than height-center by default. On a 1080x1920 canvas, use about `y=260` for drawtext cards. This keeps cards prominent while avoiding the lower subtitles and the main foreground subject. Text is large, white, 2 lines max, and centered inside a large semi-transparent dark box.
- Card background: during card display, blur and darken the underlying footage so the section card feels like a foreground title. The main subject may be blurred behind the card.
- Card motion: section cards must visibly ease in and ease out. Use about 0.7-0.9 seconds of opacity fade on entry and exit, preferably ease-in/ease-out rather than linear. Extend blur/dim timing slightly before and after the card so the transition does not feel like a hard cut.
- Subtitles: visible subtitle text should not show Chinese punctuation such as `。`, `；`, or trailing comma-like marks. It is acceptable for `narration.txt` to contain commas for TTS pacing, but render subtitles with display punctuation removed. Keep Arabic numerals visible, e.g. `1`, `128 GB`, `3D`.
- Subtitle source rule: even if visible punctuation is removed, the exact subtitle report must still reconstruct `narration.txt`. Use a separate display-cleaning layer rather than changing subtitle verification.
- Visual framing: for official horizontal keynote footage, use a 16:9 stage window on a black 9:16 canvas rather than center-cropping the speaker. This keeps faces and slides visible.
- Output naming: when iterating, save clearly versioned MP4s in `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/outputs/`, e.g. `<project_slug>_v6_visible_fade_cards.mp4`, and update `outputs/final.mp4` when a revision becomes the accepted final.

## Product-Model Visual Accuracy

Use this rule whenever Wilson asks for a video about a specific product model, e.g. `ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro`, `RTX 5090`, or any named SKU.

- Treat the exact product model as a hard visual constraint. Do not use photos, product renders, official videos, B-roll, thumbnails, gallery images, or screenshots of another product model as if they show the requested model.
- Same brand, same series, same category, predecessor/successor products, or visually similar products are not acceptable substitutes unless Wilson explicitly approves them for context.
- Do not use unrelated product footage to "represent" the requested product. Generic context B-roll is allowed only when the narration is about a generic situation, such as home networking, gaming, data centers, manufacturing, or user behavior, and it must not imply that the visible product is the named model.
- When searching local素材, filter by exact model name, SKU, official filename/metadata, visible product markings, source page, or a confirmed official asset URL. If the match is only thematic or approximate, mark it as context B-roll, not product footage.
- If model identity is uncertain, stop before final editing and send Wilson screenshots or still frames for confirmation. Include the source path or URL and state what is uncertain, e.g. `這張可能是 GT-BE98 Pro，不確定是否可當 GT-BN98 Pro 視覺`.
- In the `Frame 對照草圖`, label each planned visual source as one of:
  - `Exact model`: confirmed requested product model.
  - `Official context`: official brand/product-page context asset that does not show a different model as the named product.
  - `Generic context`: non-product B-roll for environment/use case only.
  - `Needs Wilson confirmation`: uncertain model identity; do not use until approved.
- Reject any final export where an unapproved different model appears during narration that names the requested model or discusses its physical design, ports, specs, appearance, accessories, or product-specific features.

## Workflow

1. Clarify only if necessary. If Wilson assigns a topic, proceed.
2. For current/news/product topics, browse and cite current primary or official sources where possible.
3. Draft a concise Shorts script with a clear hook, 2-4 sections, one practical takeaway, and the Depth Standard. For strategic topics, first define the thesis, mechanism, impact, limitation, and takeaway, then compress that into short-form narration.
4. Search local materials for relevant B-roll by filename, theme, aspect, and technical quality with the maintained CSV/JSON index and direct file review. Prefer native `vertical_9x16` candidates, then fall back to high-quality `horizontal_16x9` sources when vertical素材 is unavailable or less relevant. For important videos, give Wilson 5-8 candidate素材 choices before final editing when time allows or when the request is subjective.
5. Download or capture web/news/product visuals into the work folder.
6. Present the `大綱`, `逐字稿`, and `Frame 對照草圖` for Wilson approval. Stop until approved.
7. Build the mixed-visual edit timeline, subtitles, cards, and visual layout using draft/silent timing or estimated narration timing. Do not call ElevenLabs or Gemini TTS yet.
8. Run local visual/subtitle/card QA on the silent or draft-timed video and fix layout issues before TTS.
9. After Wilson approval and local video/subtitle/card QA, generate ElevenLabs TTS once from exactly `narration.txt`, using `ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID=eleven_v3` and `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID`; if ElevenLabs is unavailable, generate one Google/Gemini fallback TTS using `Orus`.
10. Reconcile final audio duration with subtitle timing by aligning subtitle segment starts/ends to the actual TTS waveform and pauses, then attach narration, mix audio, and make only timing adjustments needed to prevent truncation or subtitle drift. Do not use this phase for major script or visual redesign unless Wilson re-approves.
11. Visual rules for the mixed edit:
   - Visual relevance is mandatory. Match visuals to the narration beat: when the narration says notebook/laptop, use laptop footage; when it says GPU/platform/CUDA, use GPU, developer, Windows, or AI-workflow footage; when it says cloud/data center, use server/data-center/cloud visuals; when it says competitors, use appropriate chip/platform visuals. Do not fill a segment with unrelated keynote shots that are visually hard to understand.
   - Web/news images: use smooth Ken Burns motion only for static photos or static screenshots. Avoid FFmpeg `zoompan` at plain 30fps because it can look jittery. Prefer pre-scaling images larger than canvas, animating crop/pan/zoom with gentle easing at 60fps, then outputting final video at 30fps; if this still looks rough, use slower dissolves plus nearby B-roll instead of forced movement.
   - Videos and animations: never apply Ken Burns or artificial still-image pan/zoom to footage that already has motion. Use clean cuts, trims, speed-neutral playback, or subtle scale-to-fit framing only.
   - Title cards, theme pages, and section cards: do not apply Ken Burns. Use static composition plus intentional fades/ease transitions only.
   - Local videos: use vertical framing with blurred fill background and centered foreground.
   - Do not loop or replay the same local B-roll clip as filler. Reusing the same source path with the same `source_start` makes the rendered Short visibly restart the same moment; treat that as a QA failure. If a source must appear again, use a clearly different timestamp/shot and only when editorially justified, otherwise choose a different素材.
   - Add short key-word cards only as emphasis; they must not replace complete subtitles.
   - For keynote/product-launch topics, use the approved v8 keynote style when relevant:
     - Prefer short 2-7 second visual cuts, especially around speaker shots, product closeups, slide reveals, audience shots, and local B-roll reaction/context shots.
     - Use the Approved Section-Card Template for major beat changes. Avoid opening cards and avoid excessive spec/takeaway punch cards.
     - Sync every section card to the corresponding subtitle event. Do not hard-code card times by intuition when subtitle event times are available.
     - Keep section cards rhythmic and bold, but never let them replace the exact subtitles. Subtitles remain the full narration source of truth.
     - Put the full video title or core thesis as a clean one-line top title, not only in tiny top nav text and not in a boxed persistent card.
     - Place primary Chinese subtitles lower and closer to the bottom safe area than older v6/v7 style, with optional small English below.
     - Write narration in a more conversational Shorts style, while preserving factual accuracy, analytical depth, and WilsonSpeak's professional tone.
     - Use quick but clean motion: subtle push-ins, hard cuts for visual cuts, and visible ease-in/ease-out fades for section cards. Avoid overly long static slides when keynote footage or local B-roll is available.
     - When using official keynote footage, show a small source label only during the actual keynote clips. Do not overlay the source label on unrelated local B-roll, generated visuals, or product screenshots.
     - The approved reference feel is the NVIDIA RTX Spark v6 visible-fade-card sample: black canvas, official keynote stage window, clean top title, low punctuation-clean subtitles, centered boxed section cards, blurred/dimmed background, and visible card fade in/out.
12. Mix audio so narration is clearly dominant:
   - Boost narration when needed, but avoid clipping.
   - Keep BGM clearly under narration but not buried: target about `-18 dB` to `-22 dB` relative music gain under speech, or use sidechain ducking so music dips whenever narration is present.
   - Use only Wilson-provided BGM; default to the provided `monks` track. Do not use external BGM.
   - If using FFmpeg filters, prefer BGM around `volume=0.10-0.14`, then apply `loudnorm` or peak limiting to prevent clipping.
   - Never let BGM compete with consonants or technical terms. NVIDIA, RTX, model names, numbers, and English acronyms must remain easy to hear.
13. Export to the project `outputs/` folder and update `outputs/final.mp4` for the accepted final.
14. QA before final response:
   - ffprobe confirms `1080x1920`, audio present, duration under 2 minutes.
   - ffprobe confirms `yuv420p` for YouTube compatibility.
   - ffprobe confirms SDR BT.709 output: `color_space=bt709`, `color_transfer=bt709`, and `color_primaries=bt709`. If the final output is tagged `bt2020`, `smpte2084`, or contains HDR mastering/content-light side data, fix the renderer or source transcode before delivery.
   - video duration is at least the narration/TTS duration; reject exports that truncate the ending.
   - exact subtitle report passes.
   - subtitle timing was generated from TTS-aligned segment times, not proportional text timing, and `TEXT_DELAY` remains `0.0` unless there is a measured muxing offset.
   - subtitle line-break QA confirms there are no orphan fragments, broken Chinese words, awkward semantic splits, or split English terms in any long/multi-line caption.
   - list-caption timing QA confirms `第一 / 第二 / 第三` and similar multi-line key-point captions do not appear before the narrator reaches the first item and stay visible long enough to read.
   - B-roll loop QA confirms no questioned source, especially typing/keyboard footage, is replayed multiple times from the same material moment. Inspect `video_manifest.json` or `render/shot_timeline.json` for repeated source path plus repeated `source_start`, then visually check the rendered cut.
   - card-sync report or manual timing check confirms every major title/punch card starts at or after the relevant subtitle/narration event.
   - for section cards, extract transition frames and confirm fade-in/fade-out is visible, not a hard cut.
   - subtitle-position check confirms Chinese and optional English subtitles are low, readable, inside safe area, and not colliding with cards or important visual subjects.
   - card-position check confirms cards are not height-centered over important foreground content; default upper placement is around `y=260`.
   - audio QA confirms narration is clearly louder than BGM on phone-speaker style playback. If BGM masks the voice, lower BGM or boost narration and re-export.
   - pronunciation QA confirms every price, large number, spec number, model name, acronym, and unit is read correctly and in Taiwan-natural phrasing before upload.
   - extract and visually inspect several frames across the video.
   - inspect image-motion clips in playback, not just still frames, and reject any Ken Burns clip that appears stuttery.
- confirm every major visual beat matches the adjacent narration. Reject exports where keynote/product footage is visually ambiguous or unrelated to the line being spoken when a more relevant local素材 clip exists.
- confirm named devices and accessories are visually close enough for the line being spoken. For TV-box topics, inspect frames for actual TV/streaming/remote/box/smart-home context; reject unrelated generic素材 even if it has acceptable aspect ratio or quality score.
   - for specific product-model videos, confirm every visual labeled `Exact model` truly shows the requested model; confirm any `Official context` or `Generic context` shot cannot be mistaken for an unapproved different product model. If uncertain, extract screenshots and ask Wilson before delivery.
   - confirm no obvious subtitle overlap or missing text.

## YouTube API Upload Workflow

Use this when Wilson asks to upload a finished Short. Prefer the local YouTube Data API uploader over YouTube Studio UI automation.

Default uploader project:

- Tool folder: `/Users/wilsondenq879/Documents/Codex/wilsonspeak_tools/youtube_upload`

Ask Wilson before public/unlisted, deleting state/files, replacing OAuth credentials, installing dependencies, or using Studio/CDP/browser automation.

Before upload:

1. After any re-render, refresh `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload/final.mp4` from the canonical `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/outputs/final.mp4`, then verify file size or checksum. Do not upload from a stale `upload/final.mp4`.
2. Run `ffprobe` QA: Shorts should be 9:16, preferably `1080x1920`, audio present, `yuv420p`, and under 3 minutes; WilsonSpeak target remains under 2 minutes.
3. Check metadata constraints: title <= 100 chars, description <= 5000 chars, combined tags <= 500 chars.
4. Run dry-run:

   - `.venv/bin/python youtube_upload.py "/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload" --dry-run`
5. If dry-run passes and Wilson asked to upload, run:

6. Use the generated `upload_state.json` as the source of truth for `video_id`, watch URL, and Studio URL. If `upload_state.json` already exists and the MP4 has changed, do not assume the YouTube API can replace the existing video's media. Create a versioned upload package and upload it as a new private video unless Wilson explicitly asks for metadata-only updates.
7. Final response should include the watch URL, Studio edit URL, `private` visibility, metadata verification status, and any API warnings.

Known verified API behavior:

# YouTube API Upload

Use the local YouTube Data API uploader for finished videos. This is the default and mandatory path for ordinary uploads.

Do not inspect or run old upload helpers such as `youtube_upload_cdp.py`. Do not open YouTube Studio, Microsoft Edge CDP, or native file picker automation unless Wilson explicitly asks for Studio-only settings such as monetization/ad suitability.

## Defaults

- Uploader project: `/Users/wilsondenq879/Documents/Codex/wilsonspeak_tools/youtube_upload`
- Uploader command: `.venv/bin/python youtube_upload.py "<upload-folder>" --privacy private`
- WilsonSpeak output package root: `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload`
- Urban-legend output package root: `/Volumes/Transcend/urban_legend_projects/<episode_slug>/upload`
- Confirmed WilsonSpeak OAuth channel: `Wilson說給你聽` / `UCVh09W0yeadZubifRZkYhCw`
- Confirmed urban-legend channel: `今晚Wilson說給你聽` / `UCUqxNuCwIlpMKaV3ocDVz8A`
- Default visibility: `private`. Do not use `public` or `unlisted` unless Wilson explicitly asks.
- Shorts default: do not upload SRT/captions. Shorts should use burned-in subtitles from the render pipeline. Captions/SRT upload is for long-form by default, or only when Wilson explicitly sets `uploadCaptionsForShorts: true`.
- Long-form captions require an OAuth token with `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl`. If `metadata.yaml` contains `captions:` but the current `token.json` only has `youtube.upload`, dry-run may still pass and the real upload can fail with `invalid_scope`.
- Do not automatically rerun OAuth or replace credentials to fix caption scope. If the rendered video already has burned-in subtitles and Wilson simply asked to upload, omit `captions:` from `metadata.yaml`, keep the `.srt` in the upload folder, upload the private video, and report that external YouTube captions were skipped because of scope. Ask Wilson before any OAuth scope upgrade.
- Do not upload directly from random work folders. First create a stable upload package under the per-video project folder's `upload/` directory.
- For WilsonSpeak long-form uploads, do not proceed if Wilson has not already reviewed and approved the exact narration transcript/逐字稿 in the thread or project planning files. Stop and show the transcript for approval first unless Wilson explicitly says to bypass this gate.

## Channel routing

Never assume the current OAuth token belongs to the requested channel.

- For WilsonSpeak, use the existing uploader token only when the target channel is `UCVh09W0yeadZubifRZkYhCw`.
- For the urban-legend channel, use the dedicated token at `/Volumes/Transcend/urban_legend_projects/.youtube_tokens/tonight-wilson-youtube-token.json`; do not overwrite or reuse the WilsonSpeak token.
- Put the intended `targetChannelId` in `metadata.yaml` when the upload is not WilsonSpeak, especially for `/Volumes/Transcend/urban_legend_projects`.
- Before every real multi-channel upload, call `channels().list(part="id,snippet", mine=True)` with the same token that will upload the video and compare the returned ID with `targetChannelId`. Stop before uploading if it does not match.
- Use `youtube.upload` plus `youtube.readonly` scopes for per-channel tokens that must verify `mine`; a token with only `youtube.upload` cannot prove the destination channel.

## Permission Policy

Low-risk actions may be run automatically when Wilson asks to upload or prepare a finished video:

- Inspect files with `ls`, `rg`, `find`, `sed`, and `ffprobe`.
- Create the upload package folder under `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload/`.
- Copy the finished MP4 to `final.mp4` and, for long-form, copy the selected cover to `thumbnail.jpg`.
- Write or update `metadata.yaml` for the upload package.
- Run `.venv/bin/python youtube_upload.py "<upload-folder>" --dry-run`.
- Run `.venv/bin/python youtube_upload.py "<upload-folder>" --privacy private`.
- Rerun the same private upload package when `upload_state.json` exists only for metadata/status/caption checks. The YouTube Data API uploader cannot replace the binary video file of an already uploaded YouTube video.

Ask Wilson before doing any higher-risk action:

- Use `--privacy public` or `--privacy unlisted`.
- Delete or overwrite `upload_state.json`.
- Delete videos, folders, source files, `token.json`, or `client_secret.json`.
- Re-run OAuth setup or replace Google credentials.
- Install dependencies with `pip`, `brew`, or similar package managers.
- Open YouTube Studio, use `youtube_upload_cdp.py`, use Microsoft Edge CDP, or run native file picker/browser automation.
- Change monetization, ad suitability, scheduling, end screens, cards, or other Studio-only settings.

## Package Rules

For a first upload of a Short, create:

```text
/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload/
  final.mp4
  metadata.yaml
```

For long-form videos, create:

```text
/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload/
  final.mp4
  thumbnail.jpg
  metadata.yaml
```

For urban-legend long-form videos, create:

```text
/Volumes/Transcend/urban_legend_projects/<episode_slug>/upload/
  final.mp4
  thumbnail.jpg
  metadata.yaml
```

Shorts do not require a thumbnail. If no thumbnail exists, omit `thumbnail:` from `metadata.yaml`.
Shorts do not include `captions:` by default, even if a local SRT exists in the project folder.
For the urban-legend channel, keep the cover as `thumbnail.jpg` but prefer `thumbnailFile: thumbnail.jpg` instead of `thumbnail:` unless custom-thumbnail API permission has already been verified.

If a finished video was re-rendered after a previous upload, do not expect rerunning the old package to replace the old YouTube video file. Create a versioned upload package such as:

```text
/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload/<revision_slug>/
  final.mp4
  metadata.yaml
```

Use the versioned package when Wilson says to upload the revised video. Keep the old `upload_state.json` intact unless Wilson explicitly asks to delete or overwrite it.

## metadata.yaml

### Description Policy

Do not put external links or raw URLs in YouTube descriptions by default. Write clean descriptions with the hook, episode summary, chapter timestamps, source names, and hashtags only.

- Keep full reference URLs, product URLs, download URLs, and other external links in local project files such as `research/RESEARCH.md`, `upload/source_references.md`, or project notes.
- Include external links in the public YouTube description only when Wilson explicitly asks for links for that specific upload.
- For documentary or research videos, cite source titles and institutions without URLs in the YouTube description.
- Before dry-run or upload, scan `description` for `http://`, `https://`, and `www.` and remove them unless explicitly approved.

### Tag Policy

For every upload, write a full, relevant YouTube `tags:` list instead of only a few broad tags. Target `450-490` characters for the final comma-separated tag string while staying under YouTube's 500-character combined tag limit.

Build tags from:

- Channel and brand terms: `WilsonSpeak`, `Wilson說給你聽`
- Main topic and tool names mentioned in the video
- Chinese search phrases Wilson's audience would type
- English tool/workflow variants when the topic includes English product or AI tooling names
- Format/workflow terms such as Shorts, long-form, subtitles, script, storyboard, B-roll, API upload, or automation when they are actually relevant

Do not add unrelated trending tags just to fill space. Before dry-run, calculate `len(", ".join(str(tag) for tag in tags))` and keep it at `<= 500`, preferably `450-490`. YouTube API may reject tags when only the raw tag text is under 500 but the comma-separated keyword string is over 500.

When Wilson asks to paste tags manually, return the same final tag list as one comma-separated line.

Shorts:

```yaml
video: final.mp4
uploadType: short

title: "Traditional Chinese title with #Shorts"
description: |
  Short Traditional Chinese description, key points, and hashtags.

  #Shorts #WilsonSpeak #AI

  - Shorts
  - AI

categoryId: "28"
privacyStatus: "private"
madeForKids: false
defaultLanguage: "zh-TW"
defaultAudioLanguage: "zh-TW"
embeddable: true
publicStatsViewable: true
```

Long-form:

```yaml
video: final.mp4
uploadType: longform
thumbnail: thumbnail.jpg

captions:
  - file: subtitles.zh-TW.srt
    language: zh-TW
    name: Traditional Chinese
    isDraft: false

title: "Traditional Chinese YouTube title"
description: |
  YouTube description, source names, chapter timeline, and hashtags.
  Do not include external URLs unless Wilson explicitly approves links for this upload.

  #WilsonSpeak #AI #Tech
tags:
  - WilsonSpeak
  - AI
  - Tech

categoryId: "28"
privacyStatus: "private"
madeForKids: false
defaultLanguage: "zh-TW"
defaultAudioLanguage: "zh-TW"
embeddable: true
publicStatsViewable: true
```

## Workflow

1. Identify whether the finished video is a Short or long-form video.
2. Create the upload package folder under `/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload/`.
3. Copy or place the finished MP4 as `final.mp4`.
4. For long-form, include the final cover as `thumbnail.jpg` and ensure it is under 2MB.
5. Write `metadata.yaml` using the appropriate template above.
6. Run local QA:
   - `final.mp4` exists and is non-empty.
   - Shorts: 9:16, preferably `1080x1920`, audio present, `yuv420p`, under 3 minutes and preferably under 2 minutes, no SRT/captions upload unless explicitly requested.
   - Long-form: 16:9, preferably `1920x1080`, audio present, expected duration, `yuv420p`.
   - Long-form: exact narration transcript/逐字稿 was shown to Wilson and approved before upload, or Wilson explicitly bypassed that approval gate.
   - Title <= 100 chars, description <= 5000 chars, combined tags <= 500 chars.
   - Description contains no `http://`, `https://`, or `www.` links unless Wilson explicitly approved external links for this upload.
   - Tags are specific to the video and the comma-separated tag string is close to the 500-character combined limit, preferably 450-490 chars.
   - Long-form thumbnail is 16:9 and under 2MB.
   - For non-WilsonSpeak uploads, `targetChannelId` exists and the authorized OAuth channel has been verified against it.
   - If long-form captions are enabled, inspect `token.json` scopes before the real upload. If `youtube.force-ssl` is missing, either ask Wilson to approve OAuth scope upgrade or remove `captions:` when the MP4 already has burned-in subtitles.
7. Dry-run:
   - `cd /Users/wilsondenq879/Documents/Codex/wilsonspeak_tools/youtube_upload`
   - `.venv/bin/python youtube_upload.py "/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload" --dry-run`
8. If dry-run passes and Wilson asked to upload, run:
   - `.venv/bin/python youtube_upload.py "/Volumes/Transcend/wilson_speak_projects/<project_slug>/upload" --privacy private`
9. Use `upload_state.json` as the source of truth for `video_id`, watch URL, and Studio URL. If `upload_state.json` already exists, dry-run will report `existing_video_id`; treat that as a metadata/status update path only, not as a way to replace the existing video's media file. If the MP4 has changed and Wilson wants the revised render uploaded, create a new versioned package and upload it as a new private video.
10. Final response should include the watch URL, Studio edit URL, visibility, metadata verification status, and any API warnings.

If a first upload succeeds but setting `thumbnail:` fails with `youtube.thumbnail forbidden`, the uploader may throw before writing `upload_state.json`. Recover by recording the returned `video_id`, removing or replacing `thumbnail:` with `thumbnailFile:`, verifying the uploaded video with `videos().list(part="snippet,status", id=...)`, and writing `upload_state.json`. Do not upload a duplicate just to fix the thumbnail. Report that the cover must be set manually in Studio unless Wilson authorizes another Studio-only path.

- If an existing-video update fails with `Request had insufficient authentication scopes`, do not re-run OAuth or replace credentials automatically. For a revised MP4, use a new versioned private upload package. For metadata-only edits, stop and ask Wilson before OAuth scope changes.
